subject: Re: Order form — indemnity coverage and practical ops for IP claims
messages:
From: Eli Sanders <eli.sanders@novaworks.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@novaworks.com
Date: Thu, 18 Nov 2027 11:03:00 -0500
Subject: Initial redlines — IP indemnity and claims process

Rishi,

Thanks for the call this morning. Our legal team reviewed the draft MSA + Order Form and flagged a couple of sticking points on the IP indemnity. High level:

- NovaWorks is asking for (a) explicit "right to defend" for third-party IP claims and (b) a process that requires Redwood to provide timely technical evidence and a named engineer contact for triage.
- They want a carve-out for claims arising from NovaWorks' customer-provided data and any customer-supplied fine-tuning artifacts.
- On remedies, their lead counsel is pushing for a full defense obligation (Redwood to defend, indemnify, and pay costs) subject to a $3M cap per claim; they say this is standard for their platform vendors.

I've attached the redline they sent. Can you confirm Redwood's flexibility on: defense vs. defend-and-control, the evidence/custody commitments, and whether a cap can be considered at the order-form level for this account?

If helpful, I can loop in procurement to run a mutual action plan. We have a tentative renewal window in Q1.

-Eli

Attachments: NovaWorks_MSA_redline_v1.pdf (pdf)

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Eli Sanders <eli.sanders@novaworks.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 19 Nov 2027 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial redlines — IP indemnity and claims process

Eli — thanks for the summary and the redline. Forwarding internal thoughts and an initial counterproposal attached.

Quick points up front:
- Right-to-defend: Redwood's standard position is a defend-and-control approach with notification and cooperation obligations. That said, for strategic accounts we can discuss a hybrid: Redwood will defend with reasonable cooperation from NovaWorks, but we are open to specifying a restricted set of conditions where NovaWorks may take control (e.g., Redwood materially conflicts or there is a reasoned counsel disqualification).
- Evidence/custody: we can commit to a named engineering liaison and SLA for initial evidence package delivery (48 hours for triage acknowledgement, 7 business days for a substantive evidence bundle). We need to scope the types of artifacts — logs, model config, KV cache snapshots — and agree on retention windows to avoid open-ended obligations.
- Caps: we prefer negotiating caps at the order-form level rather than the master MSA. For this account, we can consider a tiered cap: $X for IP claims tied to model outputs, higher cap for claims arising from Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct.

Attached: Redwood_MSARedline_Rishi_v1.docx (docx) — highlights proposed language and an operational annex that outlines the evidence handoff timeline.

Cc'ing Kim (legal) and Ben (account lead) to propose a quick triage call early next week so we can align on working redlines and a mutual action plan.

Thanks,
Rishi
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_MSARedline_Rishi_v1.docx (docx)

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, Eli Sanders <eli.sanders@novaworks.com>, legal@novaworks.com
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2027 10:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial redlines — IP indemnity and claims process

Team / Eli — digging in on the legal trade-offs. Notes below and an alternative clause in the attachment.

1) Defense control mechanics: Redwood can accept defend-and-control but needs: (i) Redwood choice of counsel; (ii) obligation on NovaWorks not to settle without Redwood's consent; (iii) carve-in for reasonable indemnity cooperation costs. We should avoid open-ended duty to litigate on behalf of the customer.

2) Evidence and named engineer: operational SLA is fine, but we must limit scope. Propose an "Evidence Annex" that lists data classes Redwood will provide (service logs, request IDs, aggregate telemetry, sanitized model config). Explicitly exclude customer private data and customer-supplied training artifacts. If NovaWorks needs raw training data or customer PII, they must produce it.

3) Caps and types of claims: prefer order-form cap. Proposed template: a single-claim cap equal to the MRR multiple (e.g., 12x monthly committed amount) or a flat $2M per claim with an annual aggregate. We can tier that up for proven gross negligence.

4) Notice and control timeline: Redwood to provide initial triage acknowledgement within 48 hours; NovaWorks to provide relevant customer complaint and copies of any third-party demand within 5 business days of notice. Failure to provide timely info shifts indemnity obligations.

Suggested next step: a short call (30 min) between legal + account to agree high-level principles, then we exchange clean and redline MSA+Order Form.

-Kim
Head of Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_Indemnity_Annex_Prop.txt (text)

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Eli Sanders <eli.sanders@novaworks.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 25 Nov 2027 16:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order form — indemnity coverage and practical ops for IP claims

Eli — appreciate the patience while we worked internal options. Action items and proposed MAP below: 

1) Proposed commercial compromise (Order Form): 
   - Order-form cap: $2M per claim / $4M annual aggregate as a baseline.
   - If NovaWorks elects a higher defense-control option, cap moves to $3M per claim (to reflect increased Redwood exposure).

2) Operational commitments (to include in Evidence Annex):
   - Named engineering liaison: Redwood to provide primary contact and 48-hour triage SLA.
   - Evidence package: initial logs and request-level metadata within 7 business days; deeper artifacts subject to a discovery process and a signed DPA addendum if customer PII is involved.

3) Process & timelines: 30-min triage within 48 hours of notice; decision on defense-control step-up within 10 business days; settlement decisions require joint counsel consent unless Redwood declines in writing.

4) Next steps (MAP):
   - Nov 26: NovaWorks to confirm whether they will accept the order-form cap ladder.
   - Nov 29: 30-min legal/account alignment call (link below) to agree the Evidence Annex scope.
   - Dec 3: Exchange of final redline PDFs; parties aim to sign order form during the first week of December.

I attached a draft order form that accepts the $2M baseline cap and includes Kim's proposed Evidence Annex as an attachment. If that looks reasonable, we can route for procurement approval on your side.

Thanks — looking forward to wrapping this.
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Exec, Redwood Inference
